deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a working draft of the moduli count that Riemann published in §12 of 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). The previous page sets up classes of equations F(s,z)=0 under birational transformation. The next page finishes the count and adds the p=1 caveat.

(1) Setup. Rational functions of two variables s, z bound by an irreducible equation F(s,z)=0 are 'gleichverzweigt' (equally branched) functions of s, of z, and of any rational function of s and z. So any rational function R(s,z) can serve as the independent variable. A class consists of all such systems related by this change of variable, i.e. a birational class, i.e. a compact Riemann surface X of genus p. Riemann's '(2p+1)fach zusammenhängend' means genus p.

(2) Branch points. Take the new independent variable to be a function z on X that becomes infinite of the first order at μ points. The page has 'in μ Punkten' (see corrections). Then z is a μ-sheeted cover z: X → P^1. If all branch points are simple, their number is w = 2(μ+p-1). This is Riemann–Hurwitz: 2p-2 = -2μ + w.

(3) Free constants in z. The function z contains 2μ-p+1 arbitrary constants. My gloss: μ pole positions, plus dim L(D) = μ-p+1 for a general divisor D of degree μ ≥ p+1 (Riemann's inequality / Riemann–Roch, with additive constants included in that count). This gives μ + (μ-p+1) = 2μ-p+1.

(4) Normalisation. Assume 2μ-p+1 of the branch values are independent functions of these constants. Then the constants can be chosen so that those branch values take prescribed values. Because the defining conditions are algebraic, this can be done in only finitely many ways.

(5) The count. The remaining w - (2μ-p+1) = 2(μ+p-1) - (2μ-p+1) = 3p-3 branch values are then invariants of the class, up to finite ambiguity. So a class depends on 3p-3 continuously variable quantities, the moduli.

(6) Converse (existence). If the branch values of a μ-sheeted (2p+1)-fold connected surface are given arbitrarily, there always exists a system of algebraic functions branched over that surface. This is the Riemann existence theorem. Hence the 3p-3 remaining branch values are genuinely free, and the count is exactly 3p-3.

(7) Limitation. The independence assumption in (4) holds only for p > 1. The next page notes that for p=1 the number of moduli is 1. It also suggests using an everywhere-finite abelian integral as the independent variable instead.
errors: The independence of 2μ-p+1 branch values as functions of the constants is assumed, not proved. Riemann himself flags this on the next page and restricts the count to p>1.
The constant count 2μ-p+1 needs μ large (μ ≥ p+1, D non-special) for dim L(D) = μ-p+1. This is implicit on the page.
The count is heuristic (a parameter count, finite-to-one). A rigorous moduli dimension 3p-3 came much later (Teichmüller, Ahlfors, Bers, Mumford, Deligne–Mumford).

results.what: A μ-sheeted simply-branched cover of P^1 by a genus-p surface has 2(μ+p-1) branch points
A function with μ simple poles contains 2μ-p+1 arbitrary constants
The number of moduli of a class of genus-p algebraic curves is 3p-3 (p>1)
Arbitrary branch data for a finite-sheeted surface are realised by algebraic functions
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 (rigorous later: Schwarz, Neumann, Hilbert, Weyl)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the published §12 moduli count of Riemann's 1857 Abelian functions paper. It is well known as his. The only interest is seeing the drafting process, including the explicit 'finitely many ways, since the conditions are algebraic' remark.

checkable.asserts: Branch values minus free constants equals 3p-3 moduli.
Riemann–Hurwitz for a μ-sheeted simply branched cover gives w = 2(μ+p-1) branch points.
Pole positions plus dim L(D) = μ-p+1 gives the 2μ-p+1 constants.
Hyperelliptic check: a 2-sheeted genus-p cover has 2p+2 branch points.
The naive count gives 0 for p=1, whereas the true count is 1, consistent with Riemann's caveat that the argument needs p>1.

transcription_corrections: 'Wird die Function z für jeden Punkt der Grundfläche' should read approximately 'Wird die Function z in μ Punkten der Grundfläche (s,z) unendlich von der ersten Ordnung'.
'Constanten sind so zu bestimmen, dass 2(μ+p-1)[?] Verzweigungswerthe' should read '…dass 2μ-p+1 Verzweigungswerthe gegebene Werthe annehmen'.
The insertion near the bottom reads 'die 2(μ+p-1) Verzweigungswerthe nur die' (μ, not p, inside).
'Wenn andererseits … 3 Flächen[?]' is better read as a μ-fold covering surface ('μfach bedeckenden (2p+1)fach zusammenhängenden Fläche') whose branch values are given.
'von [?] {+z+}' in the independence clause should be 'Functionen der willkürlichen Constanten in z' (cf. the next page).
